GRANT, Jr.' and 'JAMES GRANT' and give the trade; they do not say where this household lived, who else was in it, or when it came. Everything about Hubbard's later Chicago life was documented here and the date he first came was a fact everyone knew and nothing in data/sources/ stated, so it was carried as a conjecture citing nothing and left visibly empty rather than quietly filled: it was the case AGENTS.md rule 1 exists for. Hurlbut's American Fur Company chapter, read for T-0575 and cited by this record since T-0594, closes it - Montreal 13 May 1818, Mackinaw 4 July, Chicago the last day of October or the first of November - and the asymmetry that was worth leaving visible is now a smaller and more interesting one. The sentence is the COMPILER'S, not the man's: it stands outside the quotation marks in which Hubbard speaks four lines later, so a date this project had no source for at all now has a source of 1881 at rung 4, and the record says both things on its face rather than letting the citation look like an attestation. WHAT T-0753 ADDED, AND THE ONE THING IT COULD NOT. The same sentence carries more than the date T-0594 spent, and the rest of it is now on the card: `origin` reads "Windsor, Vermont, by way of Montreal" rather than the "Montreal" a careless reading of the field would have written, and the person carries a `birth_year` of 1802 with the birthplace in its note, both at the inferred grade the rung-4 layer supports and both corroborated by the man's own Calumet Club register entry of 1879. THE PARENTS WERE THE PART THAT DID NOT FIT, AND T-0849 RULED WHERE THEY GO. Hurlbut names Elizur and Abigail (Sage) Hubbard, and this dataset held no structure for them: the only relationship structure it has is the household-level `kin[]` block ratified on 2026-09-05, whose rows are reciprocal between two households IN THIS DATASET, and Hubbard's parents were living in Montreal, were never in this scene, and have no household here. The inverse must be legal; the mirror row must exist. A row with no far end is not a weaker kin row, it is one with the entire checked part removed, and a graded name with nothing checking it is a note. The second reading would also have made every genealogical name in the corpus eligible for a residents layer that reconstructs a town on one day. Cited at the Democrat of 29 October 1834, column 6; the Democrat of 12 November 1834, column 11; the Democrat of 3 September 1834, column 12. The occupation census raised reconstructed households for the trades a town of 3,265 people needed and could not document; `bookseller` was not one of them, which is why this person could only ever be ADDED and never seated on an existing record — data/research/newspapers/register_1835.json calls it `new_resident` for exactly that reason.
